short: The Restoration king, who kept his throne by never quite committing to anything.
full:
Charles II had been crowned in Scotland in 1651 and spent nine years in exile after Worcester. The collapse of the Protectorate brought him back: the Declaration of Breda promised a general pardon and liberty of conscience, and he entered London on his thirtieth birthday, 29 May 1660. It was Parliament rather than the king that then imposed a narrow Anglican settlement on the church.

His reign took in the plague of 1665, the Great Fire of London in 1666, and the humiliation of the Dutch raid on the Medway in 1667. He secretly accepted French subsidies under the Treaty of Dover in 1670 in return for promising to declare himself Catholic, which he did only on his deathbed. The Popish Plot hysteria and the Exclusion Crisis of 1679-81, fought over whether his Catholic brother James could inherit, produced the first Whig and Tory groupings. He ruled without Parliament from 1681 and died in February 1685.
